title: KTM Duke 390 vs Duke 250: Which One Should You Buy?
seoTitle: KTM Duke 390 vs Duke 250 (2026): Price, Specs & Verdict
excerpt: Compare KTM Duke 390 vs Duke 250 in terms of performance, mileage, features, comfort, price, and value for money to find the perfect KTM.
author: RideVerdict Team

image.alt: KTM Duke 390 and KTM Duke 250 parked side by side

content.text: The KTM Duke 250 and Duke 390 look almost identical in a showroom, but they feel very different on the road. Both are sharp, lightweight naked bikes aimed at riders who want performance without stepping up to a big-displacement machine. The real question is whether the extra money for the 390 is worth it for the way **you** ride.

**Quick verdict:** Buy the **Duke 390** if you ride highways often and want more power and electronics. Buy the **Duke 250** if you mostly ride in the city, want lower running costs, and prefer to save roughly ₹60,000 or more.
KTM Duke 390 vs Duke 250: Quick Comparison
**Note:** Prices and specs shown here are approximate ex-showroom figures and change by city, variant and time. Always confirm the latest numbers with your nearest KTM dealer before buying.
Price in India

The price gap is the first thing you will notice. The Duke 250 sits at roughly ₹2.1 to ₹2.2 lakh ex-showroom, while the Duke 390 costs around ₹2.8 to ₹2.9 lakh. That is a difference of about ₹60,000 to ₹80,000 before insurance, registration and accessories.

KTM recently launched the 390 Duke with a downsized 350 cc engine to keep the price lower after the GST changes. The older 399 cc motor is still sold as the more expensive **390 Duke R**, so make sure you know exactly which version you are looking at.
Planning to take a loan? Try our [Bike EMI Calculator](/bike-emi-calculator/) to see how the price difference changes your monthly payment.
Engine and Performance

content.caption: Both bikes use a punchy single-cylinder, liquid-cooled engine.

content.text: This is where the 390 justifies its price. With around 41.5 PS, it feels noticeably quicker than the 250, especially above 80 km/h. Overtaking on a highway needs less planning, and the bike stays relaxed at higher cruising speeds.

The Duke 250 makes around 31 PS. That is plenty for city traffic and weekend rides, and it feels lively from low revs. However, once you cross highway speeds, you will find yourself working the gearbox harder to keep up momentum.
Which feels better in the city?
Surprisingly, the 250 can feel friendlier in slow traffic. Its power delivery is easier to manage, and the lower output means less heat and less temptation to twist the throttle too hard.
Features and Electronics

Both bikes now come with a colour TFT display, modern switchgear and full LED lighting, so the gap in everyday features is smaller than it used to be. The 390 still has the edge when it comes to the electronics package, with a more complete set of rider aids.

items: **Colour TFT dashboard** with smartphone connectivity on both bikes
**Dual-channel ABS** on both, with the 390 offering a more advanced setup
**More rider aids** on the 390, so check the exact variant list at the dealership

content.text: Mileage and Running Costs

On paper, both bikes return a similar fuel economy of around 30 kmpl. In real life, the 390 tends to drink a little more because riders use its extra power. Servicing and insurance are also slightly higher for the 390.
To see what each bike would cost you every month, use our [Fuel Cost Calculator](/fuel-cost-calculator/) and [Maintenance Cost Calculator](/bike-maintenance-cost-calculator/).
Comfort and Handling

Both bikes share a similar chassis philosophy: lightweight, flickable and confidence-inspiring in corners. The 390 gets the more adjustable suspension, which lets you fine-tune the ride for your weight and road conditions. The 250 is slightly softer and more forgiving on broken city roads.
The riding position is sporty and upright on both. Long rides will tire your wrists a little, but short and medium commutes are comfortable for most riders.
Pros and Cons
KTM 390 Duke

pros: Much stronger performance for highway riding
More advanced electronics and adjustable suspension
cons: Power can be more than a beginner needs

content.text: KTM 250 Duke

pros: Easy to ride and friendly in city traffic
cons: Runs out of steam at higher highway speeds
Fewer electronics and less adjustable suspension
Less exciting once you get used to it

content.text: Which One Should You Buy?

items: **Choose the Duke 390** if you ride on highways every week, want room to grow as a rider, or plan to keep the bike for many years.
**Choose the Duke 250** if most of your riding is in the city, your budget matters, or this is your first performance bike.
**Stretch your budget** only if you will genuinely use the extra power. Many riders buy the 390 and never use more than half of it.

content.text: Final Verdict

**RideVerdict says:** The Duke 390 is the better motorcycle, but the Duke 250 is the smarter buy for most riders. If you are not sure, take a test ride on both. The right choice usually becomes obvious within ten minutes.
Still comparing options? Browse more [bike comparisons](/category/bike-comparisons/) to find the best motorcycle for your budget.

items.q: Is the KTM Duke 390 worth the extra money over the Duke 250?
items.a: It is worth it if you regularly ride on highways or want the stronger performance and electronics. For mostly city riding, the Duke 250 offers better value.

items.q: Which is better for beginners, Duke 250 or Duke 390?
items.a: The Duke 250 is generally easier for beginners because of its more manageable power and lower price. The 390 is faster and needs more discipline from a new rider.

items.q: Do the Duke 390 and Duke 250 have similar mileage?
items.a: Both are rated at around 30 kmpl, but real-world figures vary with riding style. The 390 usually returns slightly less if you ride it hard.

items.q: Why is there a 350 cc and a 399 cc version of the 390 Duke?
items.a: KTM introduced a 350 cc version to keep the price lower under the new GST rules. The 399 cc version continues as the 390 Duke R.
